On Sunday, October 25th we welcome Jeff […] Filed Under: Acoustic , Americana , Rock , Twangville Presents , Videos Tagged With: Jeff Black , John Hollier , Zoe Pete Ford Now & Then: Margo Cilker’s Little White Cross and the reach of The Last of the True Believers Sunday, October 18, 2026 By Tom Osborne The strongest connection between Margo Cilker and Nanci Griffith is their attention to people whose lives rarely become the subject of a song. Work brings their characters together; circumstances test how long those connections last. On Little White Cross, Cilker approaches that tradition with a particularly sobering view of American life. Griffith’s The Last of the True Believers offers a useful predecessor, showing how country arrangements and closely observed stories can give ordinary lives lasting significance. Mayfield’s Crowd Pleaser, his first full-length, was close to […] Filed Under: Acoustic , Americana , Singer/Songwriter , Twangville Presents , Videos Tagged With: Ben de la Cour , Joelton Mayfield Now & Then: The Suitcase Junket’s To Go On and the reach of Bone Machine Sunday, October 11, 2026 By Tom Osborne Matt Lorenz’s homemade instruments make The Suitcase Junket easy to recognize. His songwriting gives you a reason to stay. On To Go On, written following the death of his sister and longtime musical collaborator, Kate Lorenz, that distinction matters. Tom Waits’s Bone Machine offers a useful predecessor: a record whose unconventional roots arrangements make room for mortality and tenderness alike. As warm and comforting as the name implies, Hug embraces you like an old friend, holding space for the warmth of the past, the uncertainty of the future, and the solace of the blossoming present. Read More Spotify Apple Music Tidal Close Antonio Adolfo :: S/T 1972 Antonio Adolfo hated his 1972 solo debut. Intensely. He banned it from his official discography and denounced it whenever it resurfaced online. Yet the slightly off singing may be exactly what gives the self-titled LP its charm: there’s a Robert Wyatt or Scott Walker quality to Adolfo’s naturally dramatic timbre, with little bent edges creating tension against the jazz-inflected solos, basslines and gently cinematic arrangements. The result is a strange, beautiful record its creator wanted forgotten. Read More Close John Foxx & Harold Budd :: Translucence + Drift Music On paper, Foxx, whose own Metamatic remains a landmark of British electronic music, makes for an unlikely bedfellow for the minimalist composer. But Foxx had been listening closely: Budd’s 1984 album The Pearl had become a touchstone for his own thinking about sound and space. When they met, Foxx played Budd what he called “primitive imitations” of his music—sketches of where he imagined the sonic world of T he Pearl might lead next. Brimming with gusto and the sisters’ youthful ambition yet confident and chilling sunshine pop harmonies, the duo’s lone album is a maturely stunning accomplishment on several fronts. Offworlding: Ambient House, 1992-1997 (A Mixtape) Posted on October 12, 2026 October 11, 2026 For a fleeting moment in the early-to-mid 90s, ambient house consummated the perfect synthesis of dance music groove and cosmic expanse. The scene produced a handful of genuine superstars in the Orb and the Future Sound of London, but beneath these, there lies a whole galaxy of trippy, pulsing electronica to traverse. Here are a few hours to get you started.
